boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Folck's Mill record (August 1, 1864) in Early's Raid and Operations Against the B&O Railroad [June-August 1864]. The July 30 burning of Chambersburg, the July 31 fight at Hancock and the August 2 fight at Old Town are context and are not added. Campaign-wide marches, levies, captures, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Divisions; the live field reads zero. Kelley says the raiders were variously estimated at 2,500 to 4,500, McCausland's and Johnson's brigades, and lists his own command as three Ohio National Guard regiments, detachments of West Virginia infantry, three sections of artillery and several hundred mostly unarmed stragglers. Pond says McCausland crossed the Potomac with two brigades and four guns. NPS calls Kelley's a small force of soldiers and citizens.
claims.rationale: A range of estimates reported by the opposing commander and unit lists without counts. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: Kelley says he posted infantry and a section of artillery on the heights west of Folck's Mill overlooking the valley of Evett's Creek (as read in OCR), under cover of timber and hidden from the enemy, and that the Confederates sheltered behind the bridge, mill, house and barn. Pond places the mill three miles from Cumberland; Kelley puts the position about two miles east of the town.
claims.rationale: Ground described by an interested report and a history, with differing distances; the position was taken on the day and is not tagged inherited.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 38 total; the live field reads 60 (US 30; CS 30). Kelley says the enemy abandoned 8 dead and some 30-odd wounded; Pond says 30 killed and wounded were left on the field. No inspected passage gives Kelley's own August 1 loss; his Old Town figures of August 2 are a separate action and are not added.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap.

open_questions: Kelley's report continuation in Volume XLIII Part 1 (read, not selected), Bradley Johnson's July 28-August 3 report (No. 85, read, not selected; he says he agreed with McCausland that attacking was inexpedient), McCausland's report and the itinerary abstract remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. George E. Pond's The Shenandoah Valley in 1864 (Scribner, 1883) is a retrospective history written, by its preface, from the official documents at the War Records Office and field despatches; it quotes the reports of the commanders it describes and is not independent of them. Kelley's September 17, 1864 report, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXXVII, Part 1, is one family of interested Union accounts. The Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
